pageSubtitle: Everything you need to know about reality capture services, drone regulations, project timelines, and working with Six1Five Studio.
ctaDescription: Can't find what you're looking for? I'm here to help with any specific questions about your project requirements, technical specifications, or service details.

faqs.question: Do you have FAA Part 107 certification?
faqs.answer: Yes, I hold a current FAA Part 107 Remote Pilot Certificate, which is required for commercial drone operations in the United States. This certification ensures all flights are conducted safely and legally according to federal aviation regulations.

faqs.question: What are the restrictions for drone flights in Tennessee?
faqs.answer: Tennessee follows federal FAA regulations. Key restrictions include: maximum altitude of 400 feet AGL, maintaining visual line of sight, no flights over people without waivers, and restricted airspace around airports. I handle all airspace authorizations and NOTAMs required for your project.

faqs.question: Can you fly drones in restricted airspace?
faqs.answer: Yes, with proper authorization. I can obtain LAANC (Low Altitude Authorization and Notification Capability) approvals for controlled airspace and submit special use airspace requests when required. This process typically takes 1-3 business days depending on the location.

faqs.question: What weather conditions affect drone operations?
faqs.answer: Drone operations are weather-dependent. Flights are cancelled or rescheduled for: winds exceeding 25 mph, precipitation, fog with visibility less than 3 miles, and temperatures below 14°F or above 104°F. I monitor weather conditions closely and will reschedule if safety is compromised.

faqs.question: What's included in a typical photogrammetry project?
faqs.answer: Standard deliverables include: high-resolution orthomosaic maps, digital surface models (DSM), point clouds, 3D textured models, and measurement reports. All data is provided in industry-standard formats (GeoTIFF, LAS, PLY, FBX).

faqs.question: How accurate are your measurements?
faqs.answer: My captures are made for planning, progress tracking, and comparing one date to the next. They are not a land survey. If you need survey-grade numbers for payment quantities, boundaries, or design surfaces, I'll tell you up front, and those numbers should be confirmed by a licensed surveyor.

faqs.question: Can you integrate with existing CAD/BIM workflows?
faqs.answer: Absolutely. I deliver data in formats compatible with AutoCAD, Revit, SketchUp, ArcGIS, and other professional software. Point clouds can be directly imported into Autodesk ReCap, and I can provide specific coordinate systems to match your existing project requirements.

faqs.question: Do you provide LiDAR scanning services?
faqs.answer: Not in-house. My work is drone photogrammetry, which suits open sites, buildings, and stockpiles. If your site needs LiDAR, for example bare ground under heavy tree cover, I'll tell you up front.

faqs.question: How long does a typical mapping project take?
faqs.answer: Project timelines vary by scope: Small sites (1-5 acres): 1-2 days field work, 3-5 days processing. Medium sites (5-50 acres): 2-3 days field work, 5-10 days processing. Large sites (50+ acres): 3-7 days field work, 10-15 days processing. Rush delivery is available for 30% additional cost.

faqs.question: What factors affect project pricing?
faqs.answer: Pricing is based on: site size and complexity, required accuracy level, deliverable formats needed, travel distance from Smyrna, timeline requirements, and special permits or airspace authorizations required. Contact me for a detailed quote based on your specific needs.

faqs.question: Do you offer multi-phase monitoring services?
faqs.answer: Yes, I provide ongoing construction progress monitoring and change detection services. Multi-phase work includes a baseline capture, scheduled progress flights, and side-by-side comparisons between dates. Recurring captures are priced lower per flight than one-off visits.

faqs.question: What's your service area coverage?
faqs.answer: I'm based in Smyrna and cover Smyrna, La Vergne, Murfreesboro, and the rest of Rutherford County, plus the Nashville area and greater Middle Tennessee. Sites farther out are quoted case by case, with any travel cost listed in the quote.

faqs.question: What drone and camera equipment do you use?
faqs.answer: Primary platform is the DJI Mini 4 Pro with 4K/60fps camera and mechanical 3-axis gimbal. I also fly a DJI Air 2S. All equipment is regularly calibrated and maintained according to manufacturer specifications.

faqs.question: What software do you use for processing?
faqs.answer: I use professional photogrammetry software including Agisoft Metashape, RealityCapture, and PIX4D for data processing. Point cloud analysis is performed in CloudCompare and AutoDesk ReCap. This ensures compatibility with your existing workflows and industry-standard output quality.

faqs.question: How do you ensure data quality and accuracy?
faqs.answer: Quality checks include pre-flight mission planning with overlap checks, a sharpness check on every image before processing, and a review of each model before it's delivered.

faqs.question: Can you capture thermal or multispectral data?
faqs.answer: Not in-house. My work is high-resolution RGB photogrammetry. If your project needs thermal or multispectral data, I'll tell you up front.

faqs.question: How is my project data protected?
faqs.answer: All data is encrypted during transfer and storage. Raw imagery and processed deliverables are stored on secure, backed-up servers with access limited to authorized personnel. Data retention policies and confidentiality agreements are available for sensitive projects.

faqs.question: Do you carry insurance for drone operations?
faqs.answer: Yes, I maintain comprehensive commercial drone insurance including general liability, professional liability, and equipment coverage. Certificates of insurance can be provided to clients and their insurance companies as required for project compliance.

faqs.question: Who owns the rights to captured images and data?
faqs.answer: Clients retain full ownership rights to all deliverable data and processed outputs upon final payment. Raw imagery and flight data are retained for backup purposes according to my data retention policy, but ownership transfers to the client.

faqs.question: Can you work on secure or restricted sites?
faqs.answer: Yes, I can work on secure facilities with proper authorization. This includes background checks, site-specific safety training, escort requirements, and modified data handling procedures as needed. Additional time and costs may apply for security compliance.
